In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when the clamp is closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be applied to a pipe 20 that is already installed and that cannot be entered from a free end.

The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 may be machined, cast, moulded or fabricated from metal or from a reinforced polymer, the material being chosen for the service environment. The hinge 16 may be a pin hinge, a pair of interleaved knuckles on a common pin, or a flexible hinge section integral with the frame, provided that it holds the frame halves in register when they are closed. Closure of the frame halves in register is relied upon by the cam drive described below, so the hinge 16 and the releasable latch 18 are arranged to bring the two frame halves to a repeatable closed position rather than merely to hold them near one another.

A plurality of jaw carriages 22 is distributed circumferentially about the closed frame. In the form shown in FIG. 1 the plurality of jaw carriages 22 consists of three jaw carriages 22 distributed about the closed frame. Three carriages define a stable seat on a round pipe without over constraining it. The synchronizing relationship described below is not limited to that number, and a clamp having more than three jaw carriages 22 is built in the same way, each additional jaw carriage 22 being coupled to the cam ring by its own follower and its own oblique slot as described below.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66, which stands radially outside the cam drive described below. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10 and may be a threaded pad, a dovetail, a flange with fastener holes, or any other fitting suitable for the item to be carried. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in advancing or synchronizing the jaw carriages 22. A load applied to the mounting boss 66 is therefore reacted through the frame and into the jaw pads, and is not carried by the cam drive, so a moment applied by a carried instrument does not disturb the setting of the jaws.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 may be a rectangular slideway, a pair of parallel rails, or a bore that receives a cylindrical shank of the jaw carriage 22, and it constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame. Two of the radial guides 24 are formed in one of the frame halves and the remaining radial guide 24 is formed in the other frame half in the illustrated form, so that each frame half carries at least one jaw carriage 22 and each frame half is loaded by the clamping action.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement about a pad axis and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the concave bearing surface aligns itself with the surface of the pipe 20 that it meets, and bears on the pipe over an area rather than along an edge. The split pipe clamp 10 therefore grips pipes over a range of diameters and does not require a tool specific pipe diameter. The pad axis is parallel to the axis of the pipe 20 in the illustrated form, and the jaw pad 26 may be faced with an elastomer, with a soft metal, or with a friction material where the pipe surface is to be protected.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. The carriage spring 42 may be a compression spring seated in the radial guide 24, a tension spring acting between the jaw carriage 22 and the frame, or a leaf element. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 and lift the jaw pads 26 clear of the pipe 20, so that the frame halves can be swung apart without the jaw pads 26 dragging on the pipe.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 is an annular channel of the frame, concentric with the central axis of the closed frame, that locates the cam ring 30 radially and axially while allowing it to rotate through a limited stroke about that axis. Because the annular guide 36 continues around both frame halves, the reaction to the clamping load is taken by the frame around the whole arc rather than across the split line between the frame halves. The mounting boss 66 is carried by the frame outside the annular guide 36, clear of the cam ring 30 and of the jaw carriages 22.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung fully apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

The complementary drive faces may be plain abutment faces lying in radial planes, faces inclined so that one segment end laps the other, or a tongue on one segment received in a recess of the other. What matters is that in the closed frame each pair of faces transmits circumferential drive from one segment to the other in the direction of the clamping stroke, and that the faces separate freely when the frame halves are swung apart. The coupling is made by the closing motion of the frame halves themselves, so no fastener, key or separate coupling action is required of the operator, and there is no state in which the frame is closed but the drive is not yet made up.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30, as shown in FIG. 2. The follower 40 may be a pin, a roller on a pin, or a block. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are identical in inclination and are distributed to match the distribution of the jaw carriages 22, so that a single rotation of the cam ring 30 produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. Advance of the jaws is therefore synchronized by the geometry of the oblique slots 38 rather than by successive adjustment of individual jaws, the pipe 20 is centred in the frame as the jaws close, and no jaw can be advanced independently of the others.

Where the pipe 20 is not exactly centred when the frame is closed, the jaw pad 26 that reaches the pipe first begins to centre the pipe within the frame, because the other jaw pads 26 continue to advance by the same amount until they too make contact. The inclination of the oblique slots 38 may be chosen to trade stroke against mechanical advantage, a shallower inclination giving a larger clamping force for a given drive force and a smaller radial travel for a given rotation, and the useful range of pipe diameters for a given clamp is set by the total radial travel available at the jaw carriages 22.

13	Jaw carriages and jaw pads
14	
15	Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 may be a rectangular slideway, a pair of parallel rails, or a bore that receives a cylindrical shank of the jaw carriage 22, and it constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame. Two of the radial guides 24 are formed in one of the frame halves and the remaining radial guide 24 is formed in the other frame half in the illustrated form, so that each frame half carries at least one jaw carriage 22 and each frame half is loaded by the clamping action.
16	
17	Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement about a pad axis and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the concave bearing surface aligns itself with the surface of the pipe 20 that it meets, and bears on the pipe over an area rather than along an edge. The split pipe clamp 10 therefore grips pipes over a range of diameters and does not require a tool specific pipe diameter. The pad axis is parallel to the axis of the pipe 20 in the illustrated form, and the jaw pad 26 may be faced with an elastomer, with a soft metal, or with a friction material where the pipe surface is to be protected.
18	
19	A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. The carriage spring 42 may be a compression spring seated in the radial guide 24, a tension spring acting between the jaw carriage 22 and the frame, or a leaf element. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 and lift the jaw pads 26 clear of the pipe 20, so that the frame halves can be swung apart without the jaw pads 26 dragging on the pipe.
20	
21	The segmented cam ring
22	
23	A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 is an annular channel of the frame, concentric with the central axis of the closed frame, that locates the cam ring 30 radially and axially while allowing it to rotate through a limited stroke about that axis. Because the annular guide 36 continues around both frame halves, the reaction to the clamping load is taken by the frame around the whole arc rather than across the split line between the frame halves.
24	
25	The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame radially outside the annular guide 36, clear of the cam ring 30 and of the jaw carriages 22.
26	
27	The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung fully apart without dismantling the drive.
28	
29	The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.
30	
31	The complementary drive faces may be plain abutment faces lying in radial planes, faces inclined so that one segment end laps the other, or a tongue on one segment received in a recess of the other. What matters is that in the closed frame each pair of faces transmits circumferential drive from one segment to the other in the direction of the clamping stroke, and that the faces separate freely when the frame halves are swung apart. The coupling is made by the closing motion of the frame halves themselves, so no fastener, key or separate coupling action is required of the operator, and there is no state in which the frame is closed but the drive is not yet made up.
32	
33	Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30, as shown in FIG. 2. The follower 40 may be a pin, a roller on a pin, or a block. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are identical in inclination and are distributed to match the distribution of the jaw carriages 22, so that a single rotation of the cam ring 30 produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. Advance of the jaws is therefore synchronized by the geometry of the oblique slots 38 rather than by successive adjustment of individual jaws, and no jaw can be advanced independently of the others.
34	
35	Where the pipe 20 is not exactly centred when the frame is closed, the jaw pad 26 that reaches the pipe first begins to centre the pipe within the frame, because the other jaw pads 26 continue to advance by the same amount until they too make contact. The inclination of the oblique slots 38 may be chosen to trade stroke against mechanical advantage, a shallower inclination giving a larger clamping force for a given drive force and a smaller radial travel for a given rotation, and the useful range of pipe diameters for a given clamp is set by the total radial travel available at the jaw carriages 22.
36	
37	The latch drive
38	
39	The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke. The ring drive face 54 is presented at the latch end of the cam ring 30 and is inclined to the path of the wedge 52, so that advance of the wedge 52 is converted into circumferential displacement of the cam ring 30. The ring drive face 54 may be formed on a lug that projects outwardly from one of the cam-ring segments at the latch end, or on the end of a segment itself where the annular guide 36 is open to the wedge 52. The limited stroke is bounded by the frame, by the ends of the oblique slots 38, or by a stop face of the annular guide 36, so that the cam ring 30 cannot be driven beyond the working range of the jaw carriages 22.
40	
41	The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 closed around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20, the cam ring 30 standing at the beginning of its stroke and the jaw carriages 22 remaining retracted under the carriage springs 42. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20, and in which the line of action of the clamping load passes over the pivot of the releasable latch 18 so that the load holds the latch closed rather than opening it. The first position allows the operator to capture the pipe 20 and slide or rotate the split pipe clamp 10 to its intended station before any clamping load is applied.
42	
43	Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and an over-center link 68 connecting the latch handle 56 to the drive path that ends at the wedge 52. A force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in that drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52. The force-limiting spring stack 62 may be a stack of disc springs, a nest of helical compression springs, or a single compression spring, selected to a chosen preload and rate.
44	
45	Until all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, the force-limiting spring stack 62 transmits the drive from the latch handle 56 to the wedge 52 substantially without compressing, because the resistance of the retracting carriage springs 42 is small compared with the preload of the force-limiting spring stack 62. Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The additional latch travel that remains after contact, which varies from installation to installation with the diameter and the tolerance of the pipe 20, is therefore taken up elastically. The clamping load is set by the force-limiting spring stack 62 and not by the position at which the releasable latch 18 comes to rest, so the same clamp applies a comparable load to a large pipe and to a small pipe within its range, and a thin walled pipe is not deformed by the surplus travel of the latch.
46	
47	An indicator pin 64 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 62 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator pin 64 is carried by the movable end of the force-limiting spring stack 62 and projects through an opening of the latch housing 58, so that its position relative to the fixed edge 60 follows the compression of the force-limiting spring stack 62. The predetermined compression range corresponds to the intended clamping load of the split pipe clamp 10, and the emergence of the indicator pin 64 past the fixed edge 60 is a visible mechanical report that the clamp is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20. No electrical power, instrumentation or calibration equipment is required at the pipe to read it, and the report is available at the moment the latch is closed.
48	
49	Installation and removal
50	
51	To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping, and positions the split pipe clamp 10 along the pipe 20. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Remaining travel of the latch handle 56 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator confirms the clamping load by observing the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.
52	
53	To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads, the wedge 52 retreats from the ring drive face 54, and the carriage springs 42 rotate the cam ring 30 back through the oblique slots 38 and retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the hinge-end drive face 44, the hinge-end drive face 46, the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable and may be fitted, removed and refitted without tools.
54	
55	The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 may be machined, cast, moulded or fabricated from metal or from a reinforced polymer, the material being chosen for the service environment. The hinge 16 may be a pin hinge, a pair of interleaved knuckles on a common pin, or a flexible hinge section integral with the frame, provided that it holds the frame halves in register when they are closed. Closure of the frame halves in register is relied upon by the cam drive described below, so the hinge 16 and the releasable latch 18 are arranged to bring the two frame halves to a repeatable closed position rather than merely to hold them near one another.

A plurality of jaw carriages 22 is distributed circumferentially about the closed frame. In the form shown in FIG. 1 the plurality of jaw carriages 22 consists of three jaw carriages 22 distributed about the closed frame. Three carriages define a stable seat on a round pipe without over constraining it. The synchronizing relationship described below is not limited to that number, and a clamp having more than three jaw carriages 22 is built in the same way, each additional jaw carriage 22 being coupled to the cam ring by its own follower and its own oblique slot as described below.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66, which stands radially outside the cam drive described below. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10 and may be a threaded pad, a dovetail, a flange with fastener holes, or any other fitting suitable for the item to be carried. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in advancing or synchronizing the jaw carriages 22. A load applied to the mounting boss 66 is therefore reacted through the frame and into the jaw pads, and is not carried by the cam drive, so a moment applied by a carried instrument does not disturb the setting of the jaws.

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 may be a rectangular slideway, a pair of parallel rails, or a bore that receives a cylindrical shank of the jaw carriage 22, and it constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame. Two of the radial guides 24 are formed in one of the frame halves and the remaining radial guide 24 is formed in the other frame half in the illustrated form, so that each frame half carries at least one jaw carriage 22 and each frame half is loaded by the clamping action.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement about a pad axis and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the concave bearing surface aligns itself with the surface of the pipe 20 that it meets, and bears on the pipe over an area rather than along an edge. The split pipe clamp 10 therefore grips pipes over a range of diameters and does not require a tool specific pipe diameter. The pad axis is parallel to the axis of the pipe 20 in the illustrated form, and the jaw pad 26 may be faced with an elastomer, with a soft metal, or with a friction material where the pipe surface is to be protected.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. The carriage spring 42 may be a compression spring seated in the radial guide 24, a tension spring acting between the jaw carriage 22 and the frame, or a leaf element. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 and lift the jaw pads 26 clear of the pipe 20, so that the frame halves can be swung apart without the jaw pads 26 dragging on the pipe.

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 is an annular channel of the frame, concentric with the central axis of the closed frame, that locates the cam ring 30 radially and axially while allowing it to rotate through a limited stroke about that axis. Because the annular guide 36 continues around both frame halves, the reaction to the clamping load is taken by the frame around the whole arc rather than across the split line between the frame halves.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame radially outside the annular guide 36, clear of the cam ring 30 and of the jaw carriages 22.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung fully apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

The complementary drive faces may be plain abutment faces lying in radial planes, faces inclined so that one segment end laps the other, or a tongue on one segment received in a recess of the other. What matters is that in the closed frame each pair of faces transmits circumferential drive from one segment to the other in the direction of the clamping stroke, and that the faces separate freely when the frame halves are swung apart. The coupling is made by the closing motion of the frame halves themselves, so no fastener, key or separate coupling action is required of the operator, and there is no state in which the frame is closed but the drive is not yet made up.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30, as shown in FIG. 2. The follower 40 may be a pin, a roller on a pin, or a block. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are identical in inclination and are distributed to match the distribution of the jaw carriages 22, so that a single rotation of the cam ring 30 produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. Advance of the jaws is therefore synchronized by the geometry of the oblique slots 38 rather than by successive adjustment of individual jaws, and no jaw can be advanced independently of the others.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke. The ring drive face 54 is presented at the latch end of the cam ring 30 and is inclined to the path of the wedge 52, so that advance of the wedge 52 is converted into circumferential displacement of the cam ring 30. The ring drive face 54 may be formed on a lug that projects outwardly from one of the cam-ring segments at the latch end, or on the end of a segment itself where the annular guide 36 is open to the wedge 52. The limited stroke is bounded by the frame, by the ends of the oblique slots 38, or by a stop face of the annular guide 36, so that the cam ring 30 cannot be driven beyond the working range of the jaw carriages 22.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 closed around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20, the cam ring 30 standing at the beginning of its stroke and the jaw carriages 22 remaining retracted under the carriage springs 42. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20, and in which the line of action of the clamping load passes over the pivot of the releasable latch 18 so that the load holds the latch closed rather than opening it. The first position allows the operator to capture the pipe 20 and slide or rotate the split pipe clamp 10 to its intended station before any clamping load is applied.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and an over-center link 68 connecting the latch handle 56 to the drive path that ends at the wedge 52. A force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in that drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52. The force-limiting spring stack 62 may be a stack of disc springs, a nest of helical compression springs, or a single compression spring, selected to a chosen preload and rate.

Until all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, the force-limiting spring stack 62 transmits the drive from the latch handle 56 to the wedge 52 substantially without compressing, because the resistance of the retracting carriage springs 42 is small compared with the preload of the force-limiting spring stack 62. Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The additional latch travel that remains after contact, which varies from installation to installation with the diameter and the tolerance of the pipe 20, is therefore taken up elastically. The clamping load is set by the force-limiting spring stack 62 and not by the position at which the releasable latch 18 comes to rest, so the same clamp applies a comparable load to a large pipe and to a small pipe within its range, and a thin walled pipe is not deformed by the surplus travel of the latch.

An indicator pin 64 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 62 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator pin 64 is carried by the movable end of the force-limiting spring stack 62 and projects through an opening of the latch housing 58, so that its position relative to the fixed edge 60 follows the compression of the force-limiting spring stack 62. The predetermined compression range corresponds to the intended clamping load of the split pipe clamp 10, and the emergence of the indicator pin 64 past the fixed edge 60 is a visible mechanical report that the clamp is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20. No electrical power, instrumentation or calibration equipment is required at the pipe to read it, and the report is available at the moment the latch is closed.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping, and positions the split pipe clamp 10 along the pipe 20. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Remaining travel of the latch handle 56 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator confirms the clamping load by observing the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable and may be fitted, removed and refitted without tools.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 is an annular channel of the frame, concentric with the central axis of the closed frame, that locates the cam ring 30 radially and axially while allowing it to rotate through a limited stroke about that axis. Because the annular guide 36 continues around both frame halves, the reaction to the clamping load is taken by the frame around the whole arc rather than across the split line between the frame halves.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame radially outside the annular guide 36, clear of the cam ring 30 and of the jaw carriages 22.

The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung fully apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are identical in inclination and are distributed to match the distribution of the jaw carriages 22, so that a single rotation of the cam ring 30 produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. Advance of the jaws is therefore synchronized by the geometry of the oblique slots 38 rather than by successive adjustment of individual jaws, and no jaw can be advanced independently of the others.

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when the clamp is closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be applied to a pipe 20 that is already installed and that cannot be entered from a free end.

The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 may be machined, cast, molded or fabricated from metal or from a reinforced polymer, the material being chosen for the service environment. The hinge 16 may be a pin hinge, a pair of interleaved knuckles on a common pin, or a flexible hinge section integral with the frame, provided that it holds the frame halves in register when they are closed. Closure of the frame halves in register is relied upon by the cam drive described below, so the hinge 16 and the releasable latch 18 are arranged to bring the two frame halves to a repeatable closed position rather than merely to hold them near one another.

A plurality of jaw carriages 22 is distributed circumferentially about the closed frame. In the form shown in FIG. 1 the plurality of jaw carriages 22 consists of three jaw carriages 22 distributed about the closed frame. Three carriages define a stable seat on a round pipe without over constraining it. The synchronizing relationship described below is not limited to that number, and a clamp having more than three jaw carriages 22 is built in the same way, each additional jaw carriage 22 being coupled to the cam ring by its own follower and its own oblique slot as described below.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66, which stands radially outside the cam drive described below. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10 and may be a threaded pad, a dovetail, a flange with fastener holes, or any other fitting suitable for the item to be carried. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in advancing or synchronizing the jaw carriages 22. A load applied to the mounting boss 66 is therefore reacted through the frame and into the jaw pads, and is not carried by the cam drive, so a moment applied by a carried instrument does not disturb the setting of the jaws.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 may be a rectangular slideway, a pair of parallel rails, or a bore that receives a cylindrical shank of the jaw carriage 22, and it constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame. In the illustrated form two of the radial guides 24 are formed in one of the frame halves and a remaining one of the radial guides 24 is formed in the other frame half, so that each frame half carries at least one jaw carriage 22 and each frame half is loaded by the clamping action.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement about a pad axis and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the concave bearing surface aligns itself with the surface of the pipe 20 that it meets, and bears on the pipe over an area rather than along an edge. The split pipe clamp 10 therefore grips pipes over a range of diameters and does not require a tool specific pipe diameter. The pad axis is parallel to the axis of the pipe 20 in the illustrated form, and the jaw pad 26 may be faced with an elastomer, with a soft metal, or with a friction material where the pipe surface is to be protected.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. The carriage spring 42 may be a compression spring seated in the radial guide 24, a tension spring acting between the jaw carriage 22 and the frame, or a leaf element. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 and lift the jaw pads 26 clear of the pipe 20, so that the frame halves can be swung apart without the jaw pads 26 dragging on the pipe.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 is an annular channel of the frame, concentric with the central axis of the closed frame, that locates the cam ring 30 radially and axially while allowing it to rotate through a limited stroke about that axis. Because the annular guide 36 continues around both frame halves, the reaction to the clamping load is taken by the frame around the whole arc rather than across the split line between the frame halves.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame radially outside the annular guide 36, clear of the cam ring 30 and of the jaw carriages 22.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung fully apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

The complementary drive faces may be plain abutment faces lying in radial planes, faces inclined so that one segment end laps the other, or a tongue on one segment received in a recess of the other. What matters is that in the closed frame each pair of faces transmits circumferential drive from one segment to the other in the direction of the clamping stroke, and that the faces separate freely when the frame halves are swung apart. The coupling is made by the closing motion of the frame halves themselves, so no fastener, key or separate coupling action is required of the operator, and there is no state in which the frame is closed but the drive is not yet made up.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30, as shown in FIG. 2. The follower 40 may be a pin, a roller on a pin, or a block. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are identical in inclination and are distributed to match the distribution of the jaw carriages 22, so that a single rotation of the cam ring 30 produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. Advance of the jaws is therefore synchronized by the geometry of the oblique slots 38 rather than by successive adjustment of individual jaws, and no jaw can be advanced independently of the others.

Where the pipe 20 is not exactly centered when the frame is closed, the jaw pad 26 that reaches the pipe first begins to center the pipe within the frame, because the other jaw pads 26 continue to advance by the same amount until they too make contact. The inclination of the oblique slots 38 may be chosen to trade stroke against mechanical advantage, a shallower inclination giving a larger clamping force for a given drive force and a smaller radial travel for a given rotation, and the useful range of pipe diameters for a given clamp is set by the total radial travel available at the jaw carriages 22.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke. The ring drive face 54 is presented at the latch end of the cam ring 30 and is inclined to the path of the wedge 52, so that advance of the wedge 52 is converted into circumferential displacement of the cam ring 30. The ring drive face 54 may be formed on a lug that projects outwardly from one of the cam-ring segments at the latch end, or on the end of a segment itself where the annular guide 36 is open to the wedge 52. The limited stroke is bounded by the frame, by the ends of the oblique slots 38, or by a stop face of the annular guide 36, so that the cam ring 30 cannot be driven beyond the working range of the jaw carriages 22.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 closed around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20, the cam ring 30 standing at the beginning of its stroke and the jaw carriages 22 remaining retracted under the carriage springs 42. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20, and in which the line of action of the clamping load passes over the pivot of the releasable latch 18 so that the load holds the latch closed rather than opening it. The first position allows the operator to capture the pipe 20 and slide or rotate the split pipe clamp 10 to its intended station before any clamping load is applied.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and an over-center link 68 connecting the latch handle 56 to the drive path that ends at the wedge 52. A force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in that drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52. The force-limiting spring stack 62 may be a stack of disc springs, a nest of helical compression springs, or a single compression spring, selected to a chosen preload and rate.

Until all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, the force-limiting spring stack 62 transmits the drive from the latch handle 56 to the wedge 52 substantially without compressing, because the resistance of the carriage springs 42 is small compared with the preload of the force-limiting spring stack 62. Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The additional latch travel that remains after contact, which varies from installation to installation with the diameter and the tolerance of the pipe 20, is therefore taken up elastically. The clamping load is set by the force-limiting spring stack 62 and not by the position at which the releasable latch 18 comes to rest, so the same clamp applies a comparable load to a large pipe and to a small pipe within its range, and a thin walled pipe is not deformed by the surplus travel of the latch.

An indicator pin 64 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 62 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator pin 64 is carried by the movable end of the force-limiting spring stack 62 and projects through an opening of the latch housing 58, so that its position relative to the fixed edge 60 follows the compression of the force-limiting spring stack 62. The predetermined compression range corresponds to the intended clamping load of the split pipe clamp 10, and the emergence of the indicator pin 64 past the fixed edge 60 is a visible mechanical report that the clamp is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20. No electrical power, instrumentation or calibration equipment is required at the pipe to read it, and the report is available at the moment the latch is closed.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping, and positions the split pipe clamp 10 along the pipe 20. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Remaining travel of the latch handle 56 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator confirms the clamping load by observing the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads, the wedge 52 retreats from the ring drive face 54, and the carriage springs 42 rotate the cam ring 30 back through the oblique slots 38 and retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the hinge-end drive face 44, the hinge-end drive face 46, the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable and may be fitted, removed and refitted without tools.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

input.summary: Wrote the complete first draft of the split pipe clamp application: all ten body sections, the reference-numeral table, and four figure briefs (assembly elevation, frame interior showing the cam drive, the segmented cam ring alone, and a cutaway of the force-limited latch). Claim set is 24 claims in three statutory groupings: an apparatus independent (claim 1), an installed-assembly independent (claim 16), and a method independent (claim 19), with a graduated dependent ladder under each. Important caveat on prior art: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and the brief states that no prior-art search was run, so this draft was written with no art to design around and contains no citations. The art you were given may be incomplete, and claim 1 has not been tested against any real reference; a search should be run before filing and claim 1 may need narrowing, most naturally by pulling up the force-limiting spring stack from claim 2.
reasoning: Claim 1 is built around the one relationship the disclosure calls essential and that is structurally unusual: the cam ring is itself split, one segment travels with each frame half, and the act of closing the frame brings complementary drive faces at both the hinge end and the latch end into engagement so the two segments rotate as a single ring. That is what lets a split frame drive a full-circle cam without the operator making up a coupling, and it is the feature that would carry the claim clear of ordinary hinged band or bolted split clamps, whose tightening motion runs through the split line.

I kept the force-limiting spring stack and the indicator pin OUT of claim 1 deliberately. They are strong, arguable features, but a competitor who copies the segmented-ring-coupled-by-closure drive with a rigid latch would still infringe claim 1 as written; putting the spring stack in claim 1 would hand that away. The stack is claim 2, the indicator is claim 3, and both are recited in independent claim 16, so if claim 1 falls there is a fallback that is still worth having and an independent claim that already carries them.

Claim 1 recites 'a plurality of jaw carriages' rather than 'three'. The disclosure only names three, so I added a passage to the detailed description explaining that three is the illustrated form and that each additional carriage is coupled by its own follower and its own oblique slot in the same manner. That is a functional generalization of the disclosed mechanism, not a new fact, and it supports the plurality language; claim 7 falls back to exactly three.

Claim 16 is an installed assembly (pipe plus clamp), which is infringed by the installer rather than the manufacturer, and claim 19 is the installation method taken directly from the operator sequence in the disclosure. I did not draft a method-of-manufacture claim: the disclosure says nothing about how the parts are made or assembled, so any such claim would have needed invented process steps.

The over-center latch needed a linkage to be enabled. 1	A reusable split pipe clamp has two frame halves joined at a hinge end by a hinge and at a latch end by a releasable latch, so the frame opens around a pipe already in place. Jaw carriages distributed about the frame slide in radial guides and carry pivoting jaw pads having concave bearing surfaces. A cam ring in an annular guide is segmented, one segment travelling with each frame half, and complementary drive faces at the hinge end and the latch end couple the segments into one rotating ring when the frame closes. A wedge on the latch bears on a ring drive face and turns the coupled ring through a limited stroke, and oblique slots acting on followers advance all jaw carriages inward together. A force-limiting spring stack between the latch handle and the wedge absorbs remaining latch travel, and an indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing reports clamping load.

The dominant problem is disclosure fidelity: the inventor's disclosure and the single-message conversation are one page long and identical to one another, yet the detailed description adds a substantial layer of structure, alternatives, load paths and performance results that neither source states - an over-center link (numeral 68, claimed in claim 5), a 2-into-1 split of the radial guides between frame halves (claim 8), a pad pivot axis orientation (claim 14), a roller follower (claim 15), indicator-pin mounting detail (claim 4), stroke-limiting structures (claim 12), a drive lug on the cam ring that also drives the FIG. 3 geometry, and several asserted results (self-centering, load reaction away from the split line, spring-stack preload relationship, positioning along the pipe in the first latch position, claim 22). Ten dependent claims and one method claim rest on those additions. Claim/description terminology drift ("closed condition", "assembly", "uncoupled", "resisted") and one antecedent-basis slip in claim 9 are minor by comparison.

The candidate converts the over-center *position* into a discrete over-center *link* that is a member of the latch, gives it a numeral, claims it, and draws it in FIG. 4. Neither disclosure.md nor conversation.md mentions any link, bar or connecting member between the handle and the spring stack. This is candidate-introduced structure, and the FIG. 4 brief's "short straight bar" exists only because the draft invented it.
61	  - Suggested fix: Delete "and an over-center link 68" and the clause "and the over-center link 68 connects the latch handle 56 to the force-limiting spring stack 62" from ¶43; delete claim 5 and renumber; delete numeral 68 from numerals.md; delete the link bullet and numeral 68 from figures/fig-04.md (leaving the handle joined to the housing and the spring stack in the drive path, which the disclosure does support).
62	- **[critical] Two-guides-in-one-half / one-in-the-other distribution is unsupported, and claim 8 recites it** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶15; draft/09-claims.md claim 8) - The disclosure says only that "Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame." It says nothing about how the three are apportioned between the two frame halves, and nothing about each half being loaded by the clamping action. The candidate supplies a specific 2/1 apportionment, presents it as the illustrated form, states a consequence, and claims it.
63	  - Suggested fix: Delete that sentence from ¶15 and delete claim 8, renumbering. The disclosed statement "Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame" is already carried by ¶9 and claim 7.
64	- **[critical] Widening from the disclosed three carriages to "more than three", plus an added three-point rationale** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶9) - The disclosure fixes the count at three: "Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame." It offers no other number and no reason for three. The candidate adds both a rationale ("stable seat ... without over constraining") and an express additional embodiment having more than three carriages, which is the disclosure basis on which claim 1's "a plurality of jaw carriages" rests. Neither source supports either sentence.
65	  - Suggested fix: Delete both sentences from ¶9, leaving "In the form shown in FIG. 1 the plurality of jaw carriages 22 consists of three jaw carriages 22 distributed about the closed frame."
66	- **[critical] Jaw-pad pivot axis orientation is unsupported, and claim 14 recites it** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶17; draft/09-claims.md claim 14) - The disclosure states only that each carriage "carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe". It never states the axis about which the pad pivots or its orientation relative to the pipe. The candidate names a "pad axis", fixes it parallel to the pipe axis, and claims that orientation.
67	  - Suggested fix: Delete the pad-axis sentence from ¶17 and delete claim 14, renumbering; retain the disclosed "mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement" phrasing, which is supported.
68	- **[critical] Roller follower is unsupported, and claim 15 recites it** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶33; draft/09-claims.md claim 15) - The disclosure says only "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring." It gives no form for the follower. The candidate supplies a three-way menu of forms and then claims one of them (a roller) as a dependent limitation. The description cannot supply its own support for a detail the candidate introduced.
69	  - Suggested fix: Delete the follower-form sentence from ¶33 and delete claim 15, renumbering.
70	- **[critical] Indicator-pin mounting and housing opening are unsupported, and claim 4 recites them** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶47; draft/09-claims.md claim 4; figures/fig-04.md) - The disclosure gives only the indicator's behaviour: "A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range." It does not say the pin is carried by the movable end of the stack, that the housing has an opening, that the pin passes through it, or that the pin emerges past the fixed edge. The candidate adds all four, claims them in claim 4, and draws the opening and the projecting rod in FIG. 4.
71	  - Suggested fix: In ¶47 delete the sentence beginning "The indicator pin 64 is carried by the movable end" and change "the emergence of the indicator pin 64 past the fixed edge 60" to "the position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60"; delete claim 4 and renumber; in figures/fig-04.md delete the top-wall opening and reduce the pin bullet to a rod whose visible end stands adjacent the top wall (numeral 60 can target the top wall edge, 64 the visible rod end).
72	- **[critical] Stroke-limiting structures are unsupported, and claim 12 recites one of them** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶39; draft/09-claims.md claim 12) - The disclosure states that the latch "rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke" but never says what bounds that stroke. The candidate supplies three candidate bounding structures - including a stop face of the annular guide, which appears nowhere else in the draft or in either source - and claims the slot-end variant.
73	  - Suggested fix: Delete that sentence from ¶39 and delete claim 12, renumbering; the disclosed "limited stroke" wording is retained throughout the rest of the draft without a bounding structure.
74	- **[critical] Drive lug and inclined ring drive face added to legitimize FIG. 3 geometry** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶39; figures/fig-03.md) - The disclosure says only that "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring". It does not describe a lug projecting from a segment, does not say the face is inclined to the wedge path, and does not attribute the face to the latch-end of a particular segment. The FIG. 3 brief nonetheless draws a lug on the lower segment with an inclined flank and targets numeral 54 at that flank, and ¶39 supplies text for exactly that invented geometry.
75	  - Suggested fix: In ¶39 keep only the disclosed relationship ("Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke") and delete the inclination sentence and the lug alternatives; in figures/fig-03.md replace the lug bullet with a plain drive face at the latch end of the band and retarget numeral 54 to that face.
76	- **[critical] Asserted load path - grip reaction taken around the whole arc rather than across the split line** (draft/06-summary.md ¶1 and ¶7; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶23) - Neither source says anything about where the clamping reaction is carried, about the latch not holding the working load, or about the annular guide distributing reaction around the arc. The disclosure's statement of what the invention does is limited to coupling, driving, synchronizing and force limiting. This asserted structural result is the draft's central advantage narrative and it traces to nothing in the inventor's material.
77	  - Suggested fix: Delete the quoted sentence from Summary ¶7 and the "Because the annular guide 36 continues around both frame halves..." sentence from ¶23; in Summary ¶1 state only that the cam ring is itself split and is reassembled by closing the frame, which the disclosure supports.
78	- **[critical] Self-centering, slot-inclination trade-off and diameter-range results are unsupported** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶35) - The disclosure never states that the clamp centers an off-centre pipe, never relates slot inclination to clamping force or mechanical advantage, and never says the useful diameter range is set by total radial travel. All three are engineering results the candidate supplies. The disclosure's only statement about diameter range is that the pivoting pad bears on a pipe "without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter".
79	  - Suggested fix: Delete ¶35 in its entirety; the synchronization statement it elaborates is already fully set out in ¶33 in disclosure-supported terms.

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be applied to a pipe 20 that is already installed and that cannot be entered from a free end. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in advancing or synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 is an annular channel of the frame, concentric with the central axis of the closed frame, that retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about that axis.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, clear of the cam ring 30 and of the jaw carriages 22.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30, as shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are identical in inclination and are distributed circumferentially to match the jaw carriages 22, so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the clamping load is set by the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than by the position at which the releasable latch 18 comes to rest.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the hinge-end drive face 44, the hinge-end drive face 46, the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.
