# FIG. 2

View: front interior view of the closed clamp along the pipe axis. Patent line drawing, black on white, no shading or color. Near side frame material is omitted so the interior is open to view, a depiction convention. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

- An annular body drawn as concentric outer and inner boundary circles centered in the drawing area. The space between them is open, without hatching; the region inside the inner circle is empty and no pipe is drawn.
- Within that space, a narrow band of two concentric arcs set toward the outer boundary. This band is the cam ring, divided at two diametrically opposite locations, left and right, each division drawn as a short line across the band.
- A channel outline drawn as two concentric arcs, one just inboard of the band and one just outboard of it, in the arc stretches between the slideways, so the band visibly sits within the channel.
- Three slideways through the annular body at roughly equal angular intervals, one at the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, none at either division. Each is a pair of parallel straight lines running radially between the boundary circles.
- In each slideway a carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle, narrower than the slideway so the guide lines stay visible on both sides. Each carriage stops short of the inner circle and reaches the band at its outer end.
- On the inner end of each carriage a pad drawn as a small block whose inner edge is a concave arc curving away from the center of the view, joined to the carriage at a small circle.
- At the outer end of each carriage a small circle representing a follower, lying on the band, and around it a slot drawn as an elongated closed outline through the band, inclined so its long direction is neither purely radial nor purely along the band. The slots share one rotational sense.
- In the outer stretch of each slideway, a spring drawn as a short zigzag line joined at its inner end to the outer end of the carriage and at its outer end to the frame at the outer circle, so that it acts to draw the carriage outward.

input.summary: Every item in the review is addressed. Claim 11 no longer attributes the annular guide to the two frame halves individually: it now recites "a cam ring retained in an annular guide of the frame", matching the description and the disclosure, and the claim introduces "a frame closed about the pipe" so that both "the frame" and dependent claim 13's "outside the annular guide" have antecedent basis. The annular guide's invented channel form and concentricity statement are out of the description, which now states only the disclosed function: the annular guide 36 retains the cam ring 30 while allowing it to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame. In figures/FIG-2.md the channel outline is now drawn as two arcs straddling the band, one just inboard and one just outboard, so the sheet actually shows the retention the text cites it for, and each carriage spring is anchored at both ends, to the carriage and to the frame at the outer circle, so its drawn sense of action is outward as the description states. The three claim words the term check flagged in claim 14 are gone: the advancing step now reads "respective oblique slots of the cam ring displacing the followers so that the jaw pads pivot and seat on the pipe", and the last step reads "compressing a force-limiting spring stack ... with latch travel remaining after the jaw pads have seated on the pipe", both built from vocabulary already in the description ("displaces the follower", "compresses", "the latch travel that remains", "pivot and seat"). For the three failing drawing checks, each sheet now carries its numerals in a machine-readable front-matter list in addition to the prose declaration and the trailing list, and all three are identical on every sheet: FIG. 1 has 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 66; FIG. 2 has 22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42; FIG. 3 has 30, 32, 34, 44, 46, 48, 50, 54; FIG. 4 has 18, 52, 56, 58, 60, 62, 64. Their union is the whole 28-numeral table, no sheet carries more than eight, the four files are named FIG-1.md through FIG-4.md to match the four figures described in draft/07-drawings.md, and every brief is under the 2800-character limit after trimming wording rather than geometry. No numeral, part, embodiment or line of specification text was removed to satisfy a check, and nothing was added to the invention to accommodate a drawing.
reasoning: Claim 11 was the only place left in the document where the drive ring's guide was said to be divided between the halves. Fixing it by narrowing to 'an annular guide of the frame' costs nothing in scope that the disclosure supports, since the inventor says only that the segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. The coupling of the segments, which is what makes the claim worth having, is unaffected.

Repairing that claim created a fresh antecedent problem, because claim 11 recited frame halves but never a frame. I introduced 'the first frame half and the second frame half defining a frame closed about the pipe', which is the description's own sentence ('together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed'), and pointed the radial guides at the same frame. That keeps one name for one thing across claim 1, claim 11 and the description.

The annular guide sentence in the description was rewritten rather than deleted, because retention and limited-stroke rotation are disclosed and are what the cam drive depends on. Only the channel cross-section and the concentricity assertion went, since those were shape supplied by the draft and echoed the drawing rather than the inventor.

That deletion left FIG. 2 as the only place where the guide has any drawn form. I kept the outline there as an expressly schematic depiction convention and made it straddle the band, which is the least-specific way to show a part that retains the ring. I did not import the word channel back into the specification to match the picture.

The carriage spring bullet was changed for correctness of the depicted relationship, not for appearance: an unattached zigzag squeezed between a carriage and the outer wall reads as pushing inward, which is the opposite of the disclosed outward bias. Anchoring both ends fixes the sense of action without stating any spring form, which the disclosure does not give.

Claim 14's rewording was chosen to keep the step doing the same work. 'By action of ... until' became a participial clause using 'displacing', the verb the description already uses for what a slot does to a follower, so the claim and the description now describe the synchronizing motion in the same words. 'Taking up latch travel by compressing' became 'compressing ... with latch travel remaining', which also removes a definite article that had no antecedent.

On the three failing drawing checks, the earlier turn showed the same three failures under two different file-naming schemes, so naming alone was not the cause. What the check calls the sheet's machine-readable list is not the prose sentence the brief uses to declare its numerals, so I added an explicit front-matter numerals list to each sheet and made the front matter, the prose declaration and the trailing list agree exactly. Nothing else in the workspace is readable from here that would define the format further.

Trimming the two over-length briefs was done on wording only: shortened sentences, no removed body, contact, opening or relationship. FIG. 1 still shows the pad, not the carriage, meeting the pipe; FIG. 2 still shows all three carriages, followers, slots and springs; FIG. 3 still shows both junctions with four end faces and the plain drive face; FIG. 4 still shows the handle, stack, wedge, rod and top wall.
changes: draft/09-claims.md claim 11: 'a cam ring retained in an annular guide of the first frame half and of the second frame half' replaced with 'a cam ring retained in an annular guide of the frame'; added 'the first frame half and the second frame half defining a frame closed about the pipe' and made the radial guides guides 'of the frame' so that 'the frame' and claim 13's 'the annular guide' have antecedent basis.

draft/09-claims.md claim 14: the advancing step rewritten as 'advancing the jaw carriages inward together along the radial guides, respective oblique slots of the cam ring displacing the followers so that the jaw pads pivot and seat on the pipe'; the final step rewritten as 'compressing a force-limiting spring stack lying in a drive path between a latch handle of the releasable latch and the wedge with latch travel remaining after the jaw pads have seated on the pipe'.

draft/08-detailed-description.md: the annular guide sentence reduced to the disclosed function, 'The annular guide 36 retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame'; the annular channel and concentricity wording deleted.

figures/FIG-2.md: channel outline redrawn as two concentric arcs, one just inboard of the band and one just outboard of it, in the arc stretches between the slideways, so the band sits within the channel; carriage spring now joined at its inner end to the carriage and at its outer end to the frame at the outer circle so that it acts to draw the carriage outward; wording trimmed to keep the brief within the length limit.

figures/FIG-1.md, FIG-2.md, FIG-3.md, FIG-4.md: added a front-matter block naming the figure and listing its numerals, identical to the prose declaration and to the trailing numeral list on each sheet; FIG. 1 wording trimmed for length.
input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md still lists no references, so the draft cites none and no reference vocabulary was avoided or borrowed. Nothing in this turn changed the feature claim 1 turns on: the drive ring is divided into one segment per frame half, each segment stays with its own half when the clamp is opened, and closing the halves brings complementary drive faces into engagement at both the hinge end and the latch end so the segments rotate as a single ring, which the latch wedge then turns through a limited stroke while oblique slots convert that one rotation into common inward travel at all three carriages and the force-limiting spring stack absorbs the latch travel left over after the pads touch down. The correction to claim 11 moved the assembly claim onto the same disclosed footing as claim 1 by removing a guide-in-each-half structure the sources never state, which also removes a limitation that would have been read against the description at examination. Because no art was supplied, this positioning rests on the disclosure alone and should be re-tested against a search before filing.

Claim 11 recites an annular guide of the frame and now introduces the frame it depends on; the description states only the disclosed retaining and limited-stroke function of the annular guide; FIG. 2 shows the guide straddling the cam ring band and each carriage spring anchored so it draws the carriage outward; claim 14 uses the description's own verbs, with no 'action', 'taking' or 'until'. Each of the four sheets now declares its numerals in front matter, in the prose declaration and in the trailing list, all identical, together covering all 28 numerals in the table with no sheet exceeding eight and no brief exceeding 2800 characters.

structured_output.summary: Every item in the review is addressed. Claim 11 no longer attributes the annular guide to the two frame halves individually: it now recites "a cam ring retained in an annular guide of the frame", matching the description and the disclosure, and the claim introduces "a frame closed about the pipe" so that both "the frame" and dependent claim 13's "outside the annular guide" have antecedent basis. The annular guide's invented channel form and concentricity statement are out of the description, which now states only the disclosed function: the annular guide 36 retains the cam ring 30 while allowing it to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame. In figures/FIG-2.md the channel outline is now drawn as two arcs straddling the band, one just inboard and one just outboard, so the sheet actually shows the retention the text cites it for, and each carriage spring is anchored at both ends, to the carriage and to the frame at the outer circle, so its drawn sense of action is outward as the description states. The three claim words the term check flagged in claim 14 are gone: the advancing step now reads "respective oblique slots of the cam ring displacing the followers so that the jaw pads pivot and seat on the pipe", and the last step reads "compressing a force-limiting spring stack ... with latch travel remaining after the jaw pads have seated on the pipe", both built from vocabulary already in the description ("displaces the follower", "compresses", "the latch travel that remains", "pivot and seat"). For the three failing drawing checks, each sheet now carries its numerals in a machine-readable front-matter list in addition to the prose declaration and the trailing list, and all three are identical on every sheet: FIG. 1 has 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 66; FIG. 2 has 22, 24, 26, 30, 36, 38, 40, 42; FIG. 3 has 30, 32, 34, 44, 46, 48, 50, 54; FIG. 4 has 18, 52, 56, 58, 60, 62, 64. Their union is the whole 28-numeral table, no sheet carries more than eight, the four files are named FIG-1.md through FIG-4.md to match the four figures described in draft/07-drawings.md, and every brief is under the 2800-character limit after trimming wording rather than geometry. No numeral, part, embodiment or line of specification text was removed to satisfy a check, and nothing was added to the invention to accommodate a drawing.
reasoning: Claim 11 was the only place left in the document where the drive ring's guide was said to be divided between the halves. Fixing it by narrowing to 'an annular guide of the frame' costs nothing in scope that the disclosure supports, since the inventor says only that the segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. The coupling of the segments, which is what makes the claim worth having, is unaffected.

Repairing that claim created a fresh antecedent problem, because claim 11 recited frame halves but never a frame. I introduced 'the first frame half and the second frame half defining a frame closed about the pipe', which is the description's own sentence ('together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed'), and pointed the radial guides at the same frame. That keeps one name for one thing across claim 1, claim 11 and the description.

The annular guide sentence in the description was rewritten rather than deleted, because retention and limited-stroke rotation are disclosed and are what the cam drive depends on. Only the channel cross-section and the concentricity assertion went, since those were shape supplied by the draft and echoed the drawing rather than the inventor.

That deletion left FIG. 2 as the only place where the guide has any drawn form. I kept the outline there as an expressly schematic depiction convention and made it straddle the band, which is the least-specific way to show a part that retains the ring. I did not import the word channel back into the specification to match the picture.

The carriage spring bullet was changed for correctness of the depicted relationship, not for appearance: an unattached zigzag squeezed between a carriage and the outer wall reads as pushing inward, which is the opposite of the disclosed outward bias. Anchoring both ends fixes the sense of action without stating any spring form, which the disclosure does not give.

Claim 14's rewording was chosen to keep the step doing the same work. 'By action of ... until' became a participial clause using 'displacing', the verb the description already uses for what a slot does to a follower, so the claim and the description now describe the synchronizing motion in the same words. 'Taking up latch travel by compressing' became 'compressing ... with latch travel remaining', which also removes a definite article that had no antecedent.

On the three failing drawing checks, the earlier turn showed the same three failures under two different file-naming schemes, so naming alone was not the cause. What the check calls the sheet's machine-readable list is not the prose sentence the brief uses to declare its numerals, so I added an explicit front-matter numerals list to each sheet and made the front matter, the prose declaration and the trailing list agree exactly. Nothing else in the workspace is readable from here that would define the format further.

Trimming the two over-length briefs was done on wording only: shortened sentences, no removed body, contact, opening or relationship. FIG. 1 still shows the pad, not the carriage, meeting the pipe; FIG. 2 still shows all three carriages, followers, slots and springs; FIG. 3 still shows both junctions with four end faces and the plain drive face; FIG. 4 still shows the handle, stack, wedge, rod and top wall.

draft/09-claims.md claim 14: the advancing step rewritten as 'advancing the jaw carriages inward together along the radial guides, respective oblique slots of the cam ring displacing the followers so that the jaw pads pivot and seat on the pipe'; the final step rewritten as 'compressing a force-limiting spring stack lying in a drive path between a latch handle of the releasable latch and the wedge with latch travel remaining after the jaw pads have seated on the pipe'.

structured_output.answer: All four reviewer findings and the flagged claim terms are fixed, and the figure briefs are synchronized with the numeral table and the drawing descriptions. Claim 11 recites an annular guide of the frame and now introduces the frame it depends on; the description states only the disclosed retaining and limited-stroke function of the annular guide; FIG. 2 shows the guide straddling the cam ring band and each carriage spring anchored so it draws the carriage outward; claim 14 uses the description's own verbs, with no 'action', 'taking' or 'until'. Equal inclination is an engineering inference, not inventor support, and it appears both as a dependent-claim limitation and as description structure.

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be applied to a pipe 20 that is already installed and that cannot be entered from a free end. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in advancing or synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, clear of the cam ring 30 and of the jaw carriages 22.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30, as shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are identical in inclination and are distributed circumferentially to match the jaw carriages 22, so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the clamping load is set by the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than by the position at which the releasable latch 18 comes to rest.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the hinge-end drive face 44, the hinge-end drive face 46, the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame, which in use is substantially coincident with the axis of the pipe being gripped.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be applied to a pipe 20 that is already installed and that cannot be entered from a free end. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame, as shown in FIG. 1.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in advancing or synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame, as shown in FIG. 2. The annular guide 36 retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36, clear of the cam ring 30 and of the jaw carriages 22.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a hinge-end drive face 44 and a latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a hinge-end drive face 46 and a latch-end drive face 50. The hinge-end drive face 44 and the hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30, as shown in FIG. 2. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the clamping load is set by the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than by the position at which the releasable latch 18 comes to rest.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the hinge-end drive face 46 and the latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the hinge-end drive face 44, the hinge-end drive face 46, the latch-end drive face 48 and the latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

View: front interior view of the closed clamp along the pipe axis. Patent line drawing, black on white, no shading or color. Near side frame material is omitted to reveal the interior, a depiction convention. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

Geometry to draw:

- An annular body drawn as concentric outer and inner boundary circles centered in the drawing area, the space between them open and the region inside the inner circle empty. No pipe is drawn.
- Within that space, a narrow band of two concentric arcs set toward the outer boundary. This band is the cam ring, divided at the left and at the right, each division drawn as a short line across the band.
- A channel outline drawn as two concentric arcs, one just inboard of the band and one just outboard of it, in the arc stretches between the slideways, so the band visibly sits within the channel.
- Three slideways through the annular body at roughly equal angular intervals, one at the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, none at either division, each drawn as a pair of parallel straight lines running radially between the boundary circles.
